findings.description: The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a publicly resolvable endpoint and exposing MySQL to the internet if the subnet routing permits, greatly widening the attack surface for the database.
storage_encrypted = false disables RDS storage and snapshot encryption, leaving database data unprotected at rest on the underlying volumes and in any snapshots.

The master password is passed in plaintext via var.password and is persisted unencrypted in Terraform state (and reused in EC2 user_data) rather than being generated/managed by Secrets Manager or RDS managed master passwords.

findings.issue_category: no TLS enforcement for DB connections
findings.description: The parameter group applied to the MySQL instance omits require_secure_transport = 1, so the database accepts unencrypted client connections; the bundled PHP client connects with mysqli_connect without TLS, meaning credentials and query data cross the network in cleartext.

user_data interpolates the RDS master password (var.password) into /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user_data is stored unencrypted and retrievable from the instance metadata service, so any process or SSRF/LFI in the hosted PHP app can read the DB master credential.

The instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*". Compromise of the internet-facing PHP application on catalog_app_server yields account-wide control of S3, EC2 and RDS, enabling data exfiltration, snapshot theft and privilege escalation via ec2:RunInstances/iam pass-through patterns.

No metadata_options block is set, so IMDSv1 remains enabled (http_tokens defaults to "optional"). An SSRF in the hosted PHP application can retrieve the instance profile credentials, which carry the wildcard s3/ec2/rds policy.

No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the EBS volume that stores the database credential file /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc may be unencrypted at rest depending on the AMI/account default.

The instance is launched into portal_subnet_a with the shared portal_sg security group and the configuration outputs its public DNS, indicating an internet-facing web server; combined with the wildcard IAM role and the plaintext DB password on disk, this creates a direct path from web compromise to account takeover. (Ingress rules for portal_sg are not in this file and should be verified as restricted.)
